summary: Factory profits jump on AI demand, Hong Kong marks a year since the Tai Po fire, and a Japanese skater is booed after winning in Shenzhen.
body: China's industrial profits rose 20.1% in October from a year earlier, the fastest pace in five months and up from 14.4% in September, according to National Bureau of Statistics data released Friday.[^1] Higher demand for technology products drove much of the gain; profits for January to October were up 16%.[^1] My read: the AI boom is helping electronics makers while other parts of the economy grow more slowly.

In Hong Kong, residents gathered on Thursday to mark one year since the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, which engulfed seven high-rise blocks and killed 168 people.[^2][^3] A makeshift memorial of flowers grew through the day. Residents told The Standard about lost neighbours and homes that will have to be demolished, and asked for stable long-term housing.[^2] AP reports that the commemorations followed a government warning.[^3]

In sport, Japanese figure skater Mone Chiba says hostile fans are "not something I can control" after she was reportedly booed on the podium at the Cup of China in Shenzhen, while Russian silver medallist Alexandra Ignatova was cheered.[^4] The International Skating Union called on fans to respect all skaters. The Grand Prix Final is also in China next month, so the tone of crowds there will be watched.[^4]
